frozen_decisions_applied: Plan S5 #12: 'Ensure no new production secret is written before NVS Encryption and required key protection are verified at runtime.' -- implemented as a runtime (not build-time/Kconfig-time) check via hal_security_state_flash_encryption_enabled(), gating secure_storage_set_u32/set_str/set_blob for every namespace the Section 2.7 registry marks encryption_required, matching plan #9's exact six-namespace list.

Per Section 2.1's approved production profile (CONFIG_NVS_SEC_KEY_PROTECT_USING_FLASH_ENC=y: 'NVS encryption key sourced from the Flash Encryption key rather than a separate HMAC eFuse key block'), Flash Encryption's runtime state IS this project's NVS Encryption key-protection state -- checking esp_flash_encryption_enabled() is the correct, sufficient real signal for this specific configuration, not an approximation of a different, unchecked thing.

This project's established real-tool-grounding discipline was extended one step further than prior S5 sub-slices: this is the first sub-slice to call a genuinely new ESP-IDF *function* (not just reference a Kconfig symbol), so it was verified against a full real idf.py build inside espressif/idf:release-v5.5, not just grepped source -- confirming the real bootloader_support API actually links, not just that its declaration exists.

hal_security_state_implemented.detail: hal_security_state_flash_encryption_enabled() follows hal_identity.c's exact ESP_PLATFORM-vs-host dual-path convention. ESP_PLATFORM: wraps the real esp_flash_encryption_enabled() (bootloader_support/include/esp_flash_encrypt.h), confirmed to exist at that exact path/signature (`bool esp_flash_encryption_enabled(void);`) via a real grep inside espressif/idf:release-v5.5 before writing any code referencing it -- not assumed from memory or web search (the same discipline that caught the CONFIG_ESP32C6_DISABLE_JTAG mistake earlier in S5). Host: returns a mockable value, defaulting to false (the safe fail-closed state) via hal_security_state_test.h's SERVICE_RUNTIME_TEST_HOOKS-gated override, a no-op on ESP_PLATFORM matching hal_identity_test.h's own base-MAC override contract (security-relevant HAL state must never be test-spoofable on a real device).

write_gate_implemented.detail: SecureStorageWriteResult{kWritten, kRejectedWrongNamespace, kRejectedEncryptionNotVerified, kWriteFailed}. secure_storage_write_precondition_met(namespace_id) is unconditionally true for a namespace with encryption_required==false (Section 2.7 registry), otherwise delegates to hal_security_state_flash_encryption_enabled(). secure_storage_set_u32/set_str/set_blob apply the namespace-ownership gate (same as the Section 2.8 read path) and then this encryption-verified gate, in that order, before ever calling hal_nvs_set_*. Verified directly (not just via return value) that a rejected write never reaches hal_nvs: read the raw key back via hal_nvs_get_str/hal_nvs_get_blob after a rejected write and confirmed it remains NOT_FOUND or byte-for-byte unchanged.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: The write gate checks Flash Encryption's runtime state as a proxy for 'NVS Encryption and required key protection are verified' rather than querying NVS Encryption/the NVS Security Provider directly.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: This project's approved production Kconfig profile (Section 2.1) pins CONFIG_NVS_SEC_KEY_PROTECT_USING_FLASH_ENC=y specifically -- NVS Encryption's key material IS sourced from the Flash Encryption key in this exact configuration, so the two are the same real signal here, not an approximation. A project that later changed this Kconfig choice (e.g. to a separate HMAC eFuse key block) would need this gate updated to match.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: If this project's approved profile ever changes away from CONFIG_NVS_SEC_KEY_PROTECT_USING_FLASH_ENC, this write gate's single hal_security_state_flash_encryption_enabled() check would need a corresponding update -- not automatically kept in sync by anything in this sub-slice.
